summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with a history of diastolic heart failure, end-stage renal disease, and hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy was admitted for acute shortness of breath due to pulmonary edema. She presented with no chest pain or signs of infection, and cardiac enzymes were negative. Her symptoms were attributed to fluid overload, possibly exacerbated by dietary salt intake. She was treated with oxygen, a nitroglycerin drip, and hemodialysis for volume removal. Her condition improved rapidly, and she was weaned off oxygen by the next day. No changes were made to her home medications, though she was advised to clarify her insulin regimen with her primary care provider. She was discharged home with services, stable and ambulating with her prosthetics.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
